precepts.text: All the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens. They have no living God.
precepts.point: The mother was marvelous above all and worthy of honorable memory: she saw her seven sons slain in one day, and bare it with good courage because of her hope in the Lord. The Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man, will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again. And what kind of mercy would it be for the same people that torment us to get an equal reward in the kingdom? That is not a merciful God, if he allows them to do that to us and then they get the same portion.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

precepts.why:
The third brother, when they came to cut him, put out his tongue right away and held forth his hands manfully: come on, let's get this over with. He said courageously, “These I had from heaven; and for his laws I despise them; and from him I hope to receive them again.” And “the king, and they that were with him, marvelled at the young man's courage, for that he nothing regarded the pains.”

Why did they marvel? They had to understand there was a certain spirit in these brothers; there was something the brothers knew that the king did not. The psalm tells what it is: “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.”

All the gods of the nations are idols, so the nations have no living God. The king had power, arrogance and the fire, but his gods were dead. These brothers served the Lord that made the heavens, the God who gave them their tongues and hands and would give them again. That is why they were ready to die rather than transgress the laws of their fathers, and why the heathen could only stand there and marvel.

precepts.text: All the gods of the nations are idols. Name a kingdom that kept God's commandments; they fall because they serve idols, and Babylon the Great holds all the idols of every kingdom.
precepts.point: The desire of wisdom bringeth to a kingdom; if your delight be in thrones and sceptres, O ye kings of the people, honour wisdom that ye may reign for evermore. The only way Israel's kingdom lasts for ever is wisdom and humility toward God.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
Wisdom tells the kings of the earth that “the desire of wisdom bringeth to a kingdom”, and to “honour wisdom, that ye may reign for evermore.” David shows why the kingdoms of the nations never did: “For the Lord is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods. For all the gods of the nations are idols”.

They are all idols. All kingdoms fall because they do not walk after the wisdom of God. Name a kingdom that has kept the commandments of God. They don't. They fall because they serve idol gods, and pride destroys them, as it destroyed Herod, who gave not God the glory and was eaten of worms. Assyrian, Babylon, Greek, Rome, America: nobody is exempt from pride and God destroying them.

It is no different with Babylon the Great. This Edomite has the most gods of all: he has all the idol gods of every kingdom wrapped up in one, in different forms. That is why Obadiah follows, “concerning Edom”, the white man, the Caucasian, his biblical name: “thou art greatly despised”, and “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”. None of the kings before him, Assyrians, Babylonians, Persians, Greeks or Romans, was more prideful than Esau.

The same judgment is on us. The power God gave was given to us by God too, and for our pride as a nation we have been destroyed. The only way our kingdom will last for ever is when we walk in wisdom and humility toward God. Outside of that, the kingdom comes down, the same as it did with all the nations before us.

precepts.text: Israel did not serve the Lord with joyfulness for the abundance of all things.
precepts.point: God showed his word and statutes to Jacob and has not dealt so with any other nation.

note.label: Transforming from Immorality into Beautiful Civility Part 2

precepts.why:
“Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”. The Lord gave us the abundance of all things, and we did not want to serve him for it. So he caused us to serve our enemies, and that is why we ended up falling underneath these people. That is not where our position is supposed to be.

Before we went into captivity we were celebrating the gods of the nations, and the Lord had a problem with that. Psalms 96:5 is his message and warning to us: “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.” Our God made everything; that is the God we are connected with. So-called Christmas, Thanksgiving and so-called New Year's are pagan, evil hella days, not holy days. How can you talk about Thanksgiving on stolen land?

We are not the nations. “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel.” “He hath not dealt so with any nation”. Our customs are his statutes and judgments; we have the Bible, not idols. And Jeremiah 10 says, “Hear ye the word which the Lord speaketh unto you, O house of Israel”, “Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the heathen are dismayed at them.” Astrology, witchcraft and voodoo are the nations' problem, not ours. The Israelites are a special people, set above the nations, the jewels of God, and you have to see yourselves that way.

“For the customs of the people are vain”, void of anything credible: “one cutteth a tree out of the forest”, and “They deck it with silver and with gold”. That was the custom in the Babylonian empire, four empires before Christ was born in the time of Rome. What do lights, tin and silver on a tree have to do with Christ? Nothing. It is Sol Invictus, the unconquered sun, sun worship commemorating Nimrod, Tammuz, whom the women wept for in Ezekiel 8, celebrated on December 25th. Our people know Christ has nothing to do with it, the same way the Bible gives no white Jesus, but they will not stand up for truth.

Serving the gods of the nations instead of serving the Lord with gladness is what put us under our enemies. Anybody who continues to celebrate that madness now knows better and will be judged by the Most High.

precepts.text: All the gods of the nations are idols, but the Lord made the heavens; give unto the Lord the glory due unto his name.
precepts.point: Nebuchadnezzar came to praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, for those that walk in pride he is able to abase. The heathen understand that the Most High is greater than all other gods; it is our people that want a god that does not look like them.

note.label: Exodus 18: Jethro's Counsel and Righteous Leadership

precepts.why:
Jethro rejoiced for all the goodness the Lord had done to Israel and confessed, “Now I know that the Lord is greater than all gods: for in the thing wherein they dealt proudly he was above them.” The psalm says the same of every god Jethro measured the Lord against: “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.”

Then it calls the nations to do what Jethro did: “Give unto the Lord, O ye kindreds of the people, give unto the Lord glory and strength. Give unto the Lord the glory due unto his name: bring an offering, and come into his courts.” Jethro, a priest of Midian and not an Israelite, gave the Lord that glory: “Blessed be the Lord, who hath delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh”. Other non-Israelites came to that same knowledge.

precepts.text: All the gods of the nations are idols, but the Lord made the heavens; what Orpah returned to were idols.
precepts.point: Naomi said, Thy sister in law is gone back unto her people and unto her gods. Those gods were idols; Chemosh was the god the Moabites served.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Orpah went back unto her people and unto her gods. What were those gods? “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.”

What Orpah returned to were idols. The gods of Moab were the gods of a nation, and all the gods of the nations are idols; only the Lord made the heavens.

precepts.text: The Lord is great and greatly to be praised, to be feared above all gods, for all the gods of the nations are idols but the Lord made the heavens; there is no other God.
precepts.point: The Most High made David's feet like hinds' feet and set him upon high places, and taught his hands to war so that a bow of steel is broken by his arms, not bent but broken. He gave David the shield of his salvation and his gentleness made him great; his repentance enlarged his steps so his feet did not slip. David knew a lion and a bear were nothing to a man trained by the Most High.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“For the Lord is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods. For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.” There is no other God.

David sang, “As for God, his way is perfect; the word of the Lord is tried: he is a buckler to all them that trust in him. For who is God, save the Lord? and who is a rock, save our God?” A buckler is a shield. There is no other God save the Lord, and no rock save our God.

This is the answer to the Muslims and Negroes practicing Islam who try to make this rock into a cobblestone. It is talking about the Most High God of Israel, not a stone. The gods of the nations are idols; the Lord made the heavens.

precepts.text: The Lord is great and greatly to be praised, he is to be feared above all gods, for all the gods of the nations are idols, but the Lord made the heavens. The idols of the nations are not real; only the Most High made the heavens.
precepts.point: From midday past the time of the evening sacrifice there was neither voice nor any to answer nor any that regarded. No one answered because the Most High will not give his glory to another, and the gods of the nations are idols that are not real; they are made up by people who have no God, so when they call on them the idols cannot answer.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

precepts.why:
“For the Lord is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods. For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.”

The idols of the nations are not real. They are made up by people who have no God, so when they call on them, the idols cannot answer. Only the Most High made the heavens.

That is why, from morning until past the time of the evening sacrifice, with all their crying and cutting, “there was neither voice, nor any to answer, nor any that regarded.” There was no one there to answer.

precepts.point: Sing unto the Lord, bless His name, show forth His salvation from day to day. Why show forth His salvation from day to day? Because salvation is only for the Israelites, but your mind has to be correct, your mind has to be in the right place.

note.label: Psalm 96: Declare His Glory Among the Heathen

precepts.why:
To show forth his salvation from day to day, your mind has to be in the right place about what that salvation is. “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” Both parts were accepted by his people, the salvation and the destruction together.

Salvation is only for the Israelites, and the righteous are those keeping God's commandments. You have to accept the salvation of the righteous, and you have to accept the destruction of the enemy. If you cannot accept the second part, then Christianity, religion and God loves everybody is still in your mind, and your mind is not yet correct to show forth his salvation.

precepts.point: Bring an offering and come into His courts. Do we sacrifice? No, we do not sacrifice anymore, so the offering we bring is keeping the commandments, doing God's commandments.

note.label: Psalm 96: Declare His Glory Among the Heathen

precepts.why:
Bring an offering, and come into his courts. Do we sacrifice? No, we do not sacrifice anymore, so what offering do we bring? “He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.”

Keeping the law is offerings enough, and taking heed to the commandment is the peace offering. The offering we bring into his courts today is doing God's commandments. That is how we give unto the Lord the glory due unto his name, the honour for what he has done for Israel: he put us in slavery, and now he is bringing us back to his glory, our glory, where we once were as a people.

precepts.text: Esau is the end of the world and Jacob is the beginning; Jacob is that world that will be established and not moved.
precepts.point: He shall judge the people righteously.

note.label: Psalm 96: Declare His Glory Among the Heathen

precepts.why:
The world also “shall be established that it shall not be moved”: that is very heavy, and the world it speaks of is the world of Israel. “From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.”

Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of the world that follows. Jacob is that world, the world without end, that shall be established and shall not be moved. So when it is said among the heathen that the Lord reigneth, the world he establishes is Israel, and he shall judge the people righteously.

precepts.text: For all the gods of the nations are idols, but the Lord made the heavens; the nations' gods are nothing but stuff our God made, which he gave them to worship.
precepts.point: Fear ye not, neither be afraid; have not I told thee from that time and declared it? Ye are even my witnesses. Is there a God beside me? Yea, there is no God, I know not any. Our God stays bragging through the bible that he knows no other God.

note.label: Isaiah 44: The Idol Maker's Folly and the Changed Name

precepts.why:
“I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God.” “Is there a God beside me? yea, there is no God; I know not any.” Our God stays bragging through the bible that he knows no other God, and David tells why: “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.”

All the gods of the nations are idols. They are nothing but stuff our God made, which he gave them to worship, while the Lord, the King of Israel and his redeemer the Lord of hosts, made the heavens. So there is no God beside him, and “ye are even my witnesses” of it: he told it from that time and declared it, since he appointed the ancient people.
